invariants.title: History is evidence, not present-day authority
invariants.human_promise: Session Search may establish what was recorded in the past, but retrieved history must not silently override current Git, deployment, or other live authority.
invariants.why: Accurate retrieval of an obsolete decision can otherwise make the assistant more confidently wrong.

evidence.supports: States that session history is evidence, not semantic memory or current operational authority.
Separates historical evidence retrieval from current operational authority.

invariants.title: Accepted evidence defines the corpus
invariants.human_promise: Immutable accepted artifact bytes plus accepted-ledger membership define corpus evidence; search databases and indexes remain rebuildable derived state.
invariants.why: A mutable search projection must not be able to rewrite accepted history.

evidence.supports: Reads accepted-ledger membership and rebuilds derived corpus state from accepted evidence.
Covers accepted-ledger/projection agreement, rebuild, and reconciliation behavior.

invariants.title: Weak verification must not be reported as strong verification
invariants.human_promise: Projection consistency must remain distinguishable from full derivation verification against immutable accepted evidence.
invariants.why: A projection can be internally consistent while being derived from the wrong source.

evidence.supports: Projection consistency and full derivation verification return different bounded claims.
Checks the weaker projection-consistency contract without upgrading it to full verification.

invariants.title: Session Search remains recoverable without the current serving vendor
invariants.human_promise: Portable accepted evidence and a standalone runtime must preserve a recovery path without requiring MarcoPolo, Neon, Arcade, Google Drive transport, or a third-party Python runtime dependency.
invariants.why: Operational convenience must not silently become vendor lock-in or a single failure domain.

evidence.supports: Defines a standalone standard-library runtime with no MarcoPolo or Google Drive dependency.
Builds and consumes the portable runtime in separate hosted jobs.
Checks the portable runtime contract.

invariants.title: Runtime binding is not evidence verification
invariants.human_promise: A runtime pointer or active deployment may prove what is being served, but it must not be promoted into proof that the served projection derives from accepted evidence.
invariants.why: Operational state and evidence authority answer different questions.

evidence.supports: Separates mutable operational binding from immutable evidence authority.
Separates promotion readback from full corpus verification.

invariants.title: One stalled shard cannot hang healthy results
invariants.human_promise: A stalled or unavailable federated shard must not indefinitely block healthy shard results; the bounded response must preserve healthy results and report PARTIAL.
invariants.why: Handling an explicit error is weaker than guaranteeing bounded behavior for a request that never completes.

evidence.supports: Applies a bounded shard timeout and reports TIMEOUT.
Uses a never-resolving shard body and proves healthy results survive as PARTIAL.

invariants.title: Invalid filters fail before they distort routing
invariants.human_promise: Session and time filters must be validated before they influence shard selection; malformed inputs must not masquerade as legitimate NO_SIGNAL or PARTIAL results.
invariants.why: Otherwise invalid questions can be misreported as absence of historical evidence.

evidence.supports: Validates session/time input before routing.
Covers invalid session IDs, non-finite time values, and inverted time bounds.

invariants.title: READY means immutable searchable content
invariants.human_promise: Once a generation is READY, child searchable data under that generation identity must no longer be mutable.
invariants.why: Provenance is meaningless if the same generation identifier can point to different content over time.

evidence.supports: Requires BUILDING creation and rejects child mutation after READY.
Checks the lifecycle guard is present in the migration contract.

invariants.title: Router searches the exact generation it claims
invariants.human_promise: A router result attributed to generation X must come from a shard query explicitly bound to X, without silently falling back to whichever generation is ACTIVE.
invariants.why: Otherwise provenance labels can disagree with the data that was actually queried.

evidence.supports: Requires router_pinned_v1 witness and rejects missing or stale generation binding.
Covers missing witnesses, stale generations, and no fallback to ACTIVE.

invariants.title: Useful results retain their origin
invariants.human_promise: Search results must preserve provider, shard, generation, session/message occurrence, and relevant provenance even when presentation deduplicates repeated text.
invariants.why: Without provenance, retrieval becomes an assertion generator rather than evidence.

evidence.supports: Preserves shard/generation provenance during deterministic merge and grouping.
Checks merged/grouped results retain provenance.

invariants.title: Latest indexed time is not proof of complete source history
invariants.human_promise: Observed index bounds must not be upgraded into source completeness; without an authoritative watermark the system must preserve UNKNOWN_WITHOUT_SOURCE_WATERMARK.
invariants.why: A stale or incomplete corpus must not turn a search miss into a false claim that a conversation never existed.

evidence.supports: Carries bounded coverage/currentness semantics and the explicit unknown state.
Checks index-window and source-currentness remain separate claims.
Keeps local source currentness unknown without an external watermark.

invariants.title: Backend upgrades preserve the consumer tool identity
invariants.human_promise: Router/backend upgrades must preserve the stable TheseusSessionSearch.session_search consumer identity instead of promoting a version-suffixed sibling production tool.
invariants.why: A correct backend change is ineffective if the host selector continues choosing a different tool identity.

evidence.supports: Defines stable remote-server and consumer-tool identity across router upgrades.
Records the correction after a side-by-side candidate identity experiment.

invariants.title: Search fails closed at trust boundaries
invariants.human_promise: Public endpoint reachability must not imply search authority; router and shard use separate authentication boundaries, bounded database roles, and credential-safe error handling.
invariants.why: Functionally correct search can still be architecturally wrong if it is over-authorized or leaks secrets.

evidence.supports: Rejects unauthorized router requests before dispatch.
Rejects unauthorized shard requests before query execution.
Checks 401 fail-closed behavior.
Records least-privilege database-role readback and credential boundary.

invariants.title: Observability describes behavior, not configuration authority
invariants.human_promise: Grafana/PostHog telemetry may describe observed behavior but must not be treated as proof of canonical endpoint configuration, deployment identity, Git exact head, or accepted corpus authority.
invariants.why: A trace showing what handled one request is not proof of what is configured as canonical now.

evidence.supports: Defines Grafana as a diagnostic route and preserves service ownership boundaries.
Checks versioned dashboard structure without upgrading telemetry into authority.

invariants.title: Public research artifacts exclude private session material and secrets
invariants.human_promise: Real conversation text, raw captures, private URLs, provider identifiers, credentials, and account-specific metadata must stay out of the public repository.
invariants.why: Memory and continuity systems carry unusually high accidental disclosure risk.

evidence.supports: Explicitly forbids publishing real conversation text, raw captures, private URLs, IDs, and credentials.
Includes bounded error-redaction regression coverage.
